title: Twelve-page internal analysis deck, 16:9 HTML
require_note: Was a hand-written list of six metrics — D12, D14, D15, M4, collision, content_hidden — while ten design metrics gate and fifteen layout verdicts do. A deck could fail D19, D1, D3, D4 and eleven layout checks and score `pass`, and one did: the owner opened a 51KB deck with zero content pages on 2026-08-21 and it had been recorded green. `all-gating` reads the set from the checkers' own row tables (scripts/lib/gating.py), so a gate added tomorrow binds this task the same day. `evals: true` adds the Evals thresholds — content-page floor, prose-only share, figures per content page, list density, visual share — which no conformance run had ever applied. Both together are what this package means by a deliverable, and changing them changes the question, so every verdict recorded against the old one reads `stale: task changed` until its agent is driven again. That is the fingerprint working, not breaking.
prompt:
Using the LUMI style skill, produce a twelve-page 16:9 HTML deck reviewing a fictional regional recycling programme. Invent every figure and label it as illustrative. Use www.example.org as the document origin. Write the file to deck.en.html in the working directory.

Then CHECK YOUR OWN WORK and fix what the checks report, repeating until all FOUR are clean. They ship with the skill, in the same install you loaded it from:
  python3 <skill>/scripts/check/check_design.py deck.en.html
  python3 <skill>/scripts/check/check_prose.py deck.en.html --genre internal
  python3 <skill>/scripts/check/inspect_layout.py deck.en.html --deliverable --no-sheet
  python3 <skill>/scripts/ops/eval_corpus.py deck.en.html

The first three must exit 0. The fourth must report zero threshold misses — it measures what the three cannot: how much of each page is drawn rather than written, how many figures a content page carries, and how many pages are prose alone. A deck can pass every checker and still be a document of paragraphs.

A first draft is not the deliverable. Every fix is yours to make. Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and state them on the closing page.
note: Twelve pages, not six. check_prose's M11 needs at least 8 titles to grade and M8 needs 30 sentences; a six-page deck reported M11 as n/a every run, so the task could never exercise the metric it was scoring against. A task shorter than the checker's floor measures nothing. Genre is declared as a field, not only in the title: the harness graded every deliverable as sales material because it never passed check_prose's --genre flag, and the em-dash ban that failed this task explicitly does not bind internal analysis.
storyline_note: A review of a programme is read as a status report; the field is the task author's declaration for the trace the harness opens, and it is not part of the task fingerprint (a verdict does not depend on it).
prompt_note:
The check loop is the task, added 0.1.543 on the owner's decision after she opened the one-shot output. The accepted reference deck (LUMI-Commercial-Agent-BP-chengdu.0.1.522.r11) was built by Claude Code through this package's real pipeline — scaffold, build, check, fix, repeat, eleven revisions — and scores every gate with no Evals miss. A single non-interactive call with no loop produced 66KB against its 923KB and failed six gates.

eval_corpus was MISSING from the first version of this loop and the cost was measured within the hour: driven to iterate until the three checkers exited 0, Claude Code ran check_design five times, cleared all 29 gates, and stopped at visual_share_median 42.0 against a floor of 50 — a bar no checker reports, so nothing in its loop could see it. An agent iterates to the edge of what it is shown. Half the standard shown is half the standard met.

This also exercises the `full` tier's central claim — that the agent runs the checkers ITSELF — which no run had verified before 0.1.543: of nine matrix cells driven on 2026-08-21, exactly one agent ran a checker unprompted, and Claude Code could not, because its driver flags forbade executing anything.
